clue.text: Clues for "swan" and "gnu" get one fired shortly

parts.note: read as wordplay, SAWN OFF is an anagram clue for swan (sawn, off) and SHOT GUN one for gnu (gun, shot)

explanation.surface: A puzzle-setter hands out clues for two animal names and somehow ends up with a weapon going off.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, split up, works as a pair of clues. In SAWN OFF, 'off' tells you to rearrange SAWN into SWAN; in SHOT GUN, 'shot' tells you to rearrange GUN into GNU.
explanation.definitionFit: A sawn-off shotgun has a cut-down barrel, so it is a weapon fired from a short length, hence 'fired shortly'.

clue.text: Solitary till the end, for Narcissus?

definitions.text: Solitary till the end, for Narcissus?

parts.words: Solitary till the end, for Narcissus
parts.note: a till you work alone is one where you scan your own shopping; for the self-admiring Narcissus it is also 'checking out' himself

explanation.surface: Narcissus, lonely until his dying day, gazing at his reflection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Till' looks like 'until'; here it is a shop till. 'Checking out' also means eyeing someone up, which Narcissus did to himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A supermarket machine where shoppers scan and pay alone, with no cashier, is a solitary till.

clue.text: Spanish cheer after headers from West Ham United

indicators.note: the cheer is placed after the initials, so it comes second
headers are the tops of words, so this takes the first letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: olé is the cheer of a Spanish bullfight crowd

explanation.surface: Fans of the London football club West Ham United greet a goal with a Spanish shout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' looks like part of the club's name, but it is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Something united has been made one complete, undivided thing, so it is whole.

clue.text: Too many people spell 'phosphorus' in a bad way

parts.note: in cricket a bowler's spell is a run of overs, so a spell can be put as OVERS
P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus
someone ill is in a bad way

explanation.surface: A complaint that most people get the spelling of 'phosphorus' wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spell' looks like spelling a word; it is a cricket bowling spell, made up of overs (sets of six balls). 'in a bad way' looks like an anagram signal but gives ILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Overspill is the surplus population that a crowded town moves out to new housing elsewhere.

clue.text: Slough's fine, next to no-good part of the UK

indicators.note: the next piece is placed right beside the first

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads

indicators.note: G for good is taken away, so the word loses that letter

parts.note: England is one of the nations of the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: A cheeky claim that the English town of Slough is fine, beside some worthless region.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough looks like the town west of London; it is a bog. 'no-good' removes G from ENGLAND to give ENLAND.
explanation.definitionFit: A slough is a marshy hollow, and fenland is low, boggy country of the same kind.

clue.text: Rebuilt Noah's new ark's helm: praise be!

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together again differently, so these letters are rearranged
the helm is the front, steering end, so this takes the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Noah's ark, rebuilt and steering afresh, prompts a cry of thanks to heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rebuilt' rearranges NOAHS into HOSAN; the helm, or front, of ark's gives A.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosanna is a cry of worship and adoration of God, the same kind of exclamation as 'praise be!'.

clue.text: Bones in the foot — is heel turned over?

indicators.note: turned over in a down entry means the words are flipped and read from bottom up

parts.note: a heel is a rotten person, as is a rat

explanation.surface: A question about whether the heel bone has been flipped, asked by someone puzzling over foot anatomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heel' looks like part of the foot; it is a cad, RAT. 'turned over' reverses ISRAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarsi are the group of small bones forming the ankle and back of the foot.

clue.text: Pulling out in the air, jumper can start to gloat

parts.note: something up is aloft, in the air
a roo, short for kangaroo, is a jumper
a tin is a can

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A high-flying jumper is about to start gloating in mid-leap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' looks like a sweater; it is the Australian kangaroo, ROO.
explanation.definitionFit: Uprooting a plant means pulling it out of the ground by the roots.

clue.text: Outstanding business going places needs supply

parts.note: a loo is where one goes, so 'going places' are loos

indicators.note: read as 'in a supple way', this bends the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A business that is on the move needs to be supplied with stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a noun; it is the adverb of supple, rearranging NEEDS to ENDS. 'going places' is toilets, places you go.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose ends are details still to be settled, unfinished business that remains outstanding.

clue.text: Brad and Greg discovered off the beaten track

indicators.note: dis-covered means with the covers, the outer letters, stripped off each word

explanation.surface: Two men named Brad and Greg are found somewhere remote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' reads as 'found'; split as dis-covered, it strips the ends from each name.
explanation.definitionFit: A place off the beaten track is rarely visited, so seldom-seen or uncommon.

clue.text: Crimes reportedly why children can't go on rollercoasters

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the words are as heard, so what follows is said aloud

parts.words: why children can't go on rollercoasters
parts.note: small children are turned away from big rides for height reasons, being too short

explanation.surface: A theme-park notice explaining why small children are kept off the big rides.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'height reasons' matches the crime of betraying one's country.
explanation.definitionFit: High treason is the gravest offence against one's sovereign or state, so high treasons are crimes.

clue.text: Revolutionary sale excited football team

parts.note: Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up, so they are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A rebel gets worked up about a sale, perhaps of club merchandise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges SALE into LSEA. Chelsea is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Chelsea FC is a well-known Premier League club, an example of a football team.

clue.text: Capital Radio occasionally plugs "Rockin' Robin"

indicators.note: these letters plug a gap, filling the middle of the scrambled name
rocking letters are shaken about, so the name is rearranged
taking letters occasionally means every other one from the word

explanation.surface: The London station Capital Radio now and then promotes the old pop song 'Rockin' Robin'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital Radio' reads as one station's name, but 'Capital' is the definition on its own; 'Rockin'' gives NROBI, which takes in the plug.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital city of Kenya.

clue.text: Old spreading outbreak of lice and nasty bug

indicators.note: the old letter spreads into the middle of the scrambled insects
an outbreak breaks the word up, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An outbreak of head lice spreads alongside a nasty bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outbreak of' rearranges LICE to ECLI, and O (old) goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: E. coli is a bacterium whose harmful strains cause serious food poisoning, a nasty germ.

clue.text: Conservative's alma mater

definitions.meaning: one's alma mater is the school one once attended

explanation.definitionFit: Old-school describes traditional attitudes, and an old school is literally a former school.

clue.text: Yen to buy it?

parts.note: a yen is a longing, and to buy it is slang for getting killed, so this is a longing to die

explanation.walkthrough: 'Yen' looks like Japanese money and 'buy it' like shopping; 'buy it' is slang for dying.
explanation.definitionFit: A death wish is a desire, conscious or not, for one's own death.

clue.text: Renegade disrupted the rodeo with a kiss

indicators.note: disrupted letters are thrown into disorder, a new arrangement

parts.note: X is the cross used for a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A rebel cowboy breaks up the rodeo by kissing someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrupted' rearranges THERODEO to HETERODO.
explanation.definitionFit: A heterodox thinker departs from accepted belief, as a renegade abandons the established side.

clue.text: Children inspiring good, passion, and tact

indicators.note: inspiring in its sense of breathing in: the outer word takes the others inside

parts.note: kids are children
love is a passion

explanation.surface: Children who inspire goodness, passion and tact, like a school report's praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspiring' means breathing in here: KIDS takes in G and LOVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Handling someone with kid gloves means treating them with great care and delicacy, so the phrase stands for tact.

clue.text: "Five gold rings!" garbled aunt in country

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: the metal goes around, ringing, the scrambled relative

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: garbled words are jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An aunt mangles the line 'Five gold rings!' from the carol 'The Twelve Days of Christmas'.
explanation.walkthrough: The carol line misleads: Five is V and gold is AU, which rings NUAT, the jumble from 'garbled' aunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanuatu is an island nation in the South Pacific.

clue.text: In sum, the gutless prime minister's a relative newcomer

indicators.note: these letters go in the word sum, sitting between its letters
gutless means with the insides removed, leaving the first and last letters

explanation.surface: In short, a cowardly prime minister is a fairly recent arrival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In sum' reads as 'in short'; the word SUM itself has TE (gutless 'the') and PM put into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepmum joins a family by marrying a parent, so she is a new arrival among its relations.

clue.text: Cat close to falling in line

indicators.note: the letter is placed in the middle of the word for a line

parts.note: a tier is a row or line, as of seats

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, its last letter

explanation.surface: A cat nearly topples off a ledge while lined up with others.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiger is the largest of the big cats, an example of a cat.

clue.text: Launching unlimited new release

indicators.note: new here means made afresh, so the letters are put in a different order
with no limits, the word loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A product launch with no limit on supply for a new release.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlimited' strips Launching to AUNCHIN; 'new' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: To unchain someone is to free them from fetters, so it means to release.

clue.text: Notice German with grant

parts.note: an ad, an advertisement, is a notice
mit is German for with

explanation.surface: A notice informs a German applicant about a grant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German with' is translated as one piece, MIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To grant a point in argument is to concede or admit it.

clue.text: Part of Russia is a ruefully backwards Orwellian state

indicators.note: backwards tells you the run of letters is read from right to left
a part of the phrase is a run of letters within it

explanation.surface: Someone sadly reflects that part of Russia is a backward, totalitarian state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of' picks AISARUE from 'russIA IS A RUEfully', and 'backwards' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Orwell's novel Nineteen Eighty-Four, Eurasia is one of three warring superstates.

clue.text: Beer bottled by M&S set up in trial location?

indicators.note: the drink is enclosed, bottled, inside the other letters
in a down entry, set up means read upwards, reversed

parts.note: the letters of M&S, Marks & Spencer, a British high-street store
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Beer bottled by the British chain store Marks & Spencer, set up for a taste test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns MS into SM, which holds ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Salem, Massachusetts, is famous as the place where the 1692 witch trials were held.

clue.text: Either side of washroom being covered in dirt

indicators.note: the two sides of the washroom go round the word for either, one on each side

parts.note: or means either, as in 'either this or that'

explanation.surface: Every side of a washroom is caked in grime.
explanation.walkthrough: OR (from 'Either') sits between W and M, the two end letters of washroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A worm is a creature that lives in soil, a living thing coated in earth.

clue.text: I'll duck, after warships almost shelled American

indicators.note: the duck is put after the other pieces
almost means not quite the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: an armada is a fleet of warships
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: Someone takes cover as warships nearly shell an American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shelled' looks like bombarded; it means having a shell, armour. A cricket duck is a score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: The armadillo is an armour-plated mammal of the Americas.

clue.text: Surplus EU's saying America is behind

parts.note: a glut is a surplus
the letters of EU, the European Union, with S
a maxim is a saying
US is short for United States, America

explanation.surface: A European Union surplus, it is claimed, lags behind America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saying' looks like a homophone signal but is MAXIM; 'behind' is the buttocks, not 'lagging'.
explanation.definitionFit: The gluteus maximus is the large muscle of the buttock, the part of the body called one's behind.
